If you could go back to the early days of the internet, would you handle your privacy differently? Most of us would. We would be more careful about the services we signed up for and the information we shared. Since a time machine isn't an option, we have to face reality. Your personal data is being sold publicly right now.

Right now, your phone number, email address, home address, even your family relationships, are being packaged and sold to marketers, insurance companies, and hackers. While Safari and Mail have built-in Apple privacy protections that block some tracking when you browse, they can't erase information that has been scraped over the years and spread to hundreds of intermediary databases. Data brokers have built a multi-billion dollar industry by collecting, packaging, and selling your digital data. It's time to take your personal information off the market and the internet. Let's look at how.

The security risks of data brokers

However, the danger goes far beyond annoying spam calls. When your information is available everywhere, you become an easy target for sophisticated cyber attacks. Since this industry is essentially unregulated, your most private information and details, including past employment, where you've lived, old loans, etc., can be easily purchased. This poses a significant security concern.

Modern scammers use broker data to carefully craft highly personalized and hard-to-spot phishing attacks. When scammers already know your job title, past addresses, or the names of colleagues and friends, they can easily break through your defensive instincts. If a scammer knows you very well, they only need to strike when your guard is down, and their chances of success increase dramatically.

For those concerned about personal safety, these websites and brokers function as a searchable public database that makes it easy for harassers and stalkers to act. By mapping the network of relationships between your friends, family, and neighbors, brokers provide a targeting blueprint for people who deliberately try to stay under the radar and hide their whereabouts.

The solution: Incogni automated data removal service

This ecosystem is massive and frankly, overwhelming. Requesting removal from hundreds of sites one by one is practically a full-time job, and the success rate is extremely low, because if it were easy, these brokers would have gone out of business long ago. What you need is a solution that knows how this industry works and understands the ins and outs, to help you reclaim your right to privacy.

This is exactly why a service like Incogni has become so important to your life, both in the digital world and the real world. It takes the major headache you face (i.e., your data being everywhere and sold) and turns it into a solved problem with a one-stop approach. You don't need to spend months tracking down data brokers one by one. Incogni automatically handles those repetitive and tedious opt-out request processes on your behalf. They make sure your data isn't just removed once, but continuously maintained, because brokers will inevitably try to re-scrape and recollect your information.

Incogni's comprehensive dashboard lets you track your personal data removal progress in real time, including:

  • The number of databases that may hold your data
  • Removal requests being sent out on your behalf
  • Completed removals and items in ongoing follow-up

The real benefits of data removal for privacy-minded individuals

Removing your information from internet broker databases can deliver immediate results for you and your family.

  • When companies can't buy your number, scam calls and spam texts will decrease.
  • Scammers lose their targeting线索. Identity thieves often obtain victim information from broker websites.
  • Your home address stays private, so stalkers and harassers can't easily find where you live.
  • Your credit score stays healthy, because reduced data exposure lowers the risk of identity theft and strengthens your overall financial health.
